parts.notes: The kit's Table is a grid, and it was kept for what it gives: column and row headers, one tab stop, the arrow keys cell by cell. Its price: grid semantics on a table that is only read, and a term in a row header reached by the arrows rather than by Tab (a plain <table> would leave each term a tab stop). On a phone the table is 28rem wide and scrolls sideways under a pinned 9rem feature column, so about two plans show beside each row's name; labels wrap. The price row follows the toggle. Rows are flat (no group headings). None of it seen in a browser: unsure the pinned cells stick and cover cleanly (border-collapse draws the row's line on the tr, and the sticky cell's bg-surface is opaque), and unsure how the cell's focus ring looks on a pinned cell.

leaves.what: The term is React Aria's Button, unstyled but for a dotted underline and the kit's focus ring (src/pricing/Term.tsx), in place of the kit's Focusable around a span.

A real button gives a press: a tap shows the definition and the next tap, or a tap elsewhere, puts it away.

parts.notes: Seven terms, used in the cards' feature lists and the table's row headers; one definition each, in data.ts. Hover and keyboard focus are the kit's as documented. The press-to-toggle path (touch, Enter, Space) is reasoned from React Aria's source and was NOT run in a browser: unsure that a touch tap opens and stays open on iOS and Android, and that the 1.5s close delay never fights the toggle. The definition is tied to the term by aria-describedby only while it shows, so a screen reader hears it after focus or a press, not before. The rich tooltip's 280px maximum holds each definition.

general_leaves.what: The page: a 64dp line with the product's name, a centred heading, three sections in a max-w-6xl column.
general_leaves.why: Expected of the screen. The site-header block was not used: the screen names no header part, and its links would go to pages that do not exist.

friction: No part was seen running: there is no browser here, so everything beyond types is taken from the kit's comments and React Aria's source. (1) The doc comment that matters is not the first in Card, Disclosure, Table, Button and Badge: a reader told to read 'the doc comment first' meets a one-line comment about a context or a type and must read the file to find the real one. A file header, or the main comment at the top, would fix it. (2) SegmentedButton is the name one looks for; its comment says to use ButtonGroup instead, and the toggle recipe (Button isToggle with an id, direct children, no text variant, w-full to be constrained) is spread over two files. One example of a single-select connected group in ButtonGroup's comment would do. (3) Nothing says how to emphasise a card: whether a role pair on className is the intended way, or whether CardContent survives it (it does not: it asserts on-surface). (4) Tooltips on touch: the Tooltip comment says a touch screen gets nothing only in Table's cut-cell paragraph, and offers no term/toggletip; a page read on phones has to build one. (5) Table gives no guidance for a narrow screen or for a table that is read rather than operated. (6) No skeleton or placeholder. (7) The kit's CheckIcon and MinusIcon are exported but the skill says 'the kit ships no icon library', which reads as 'bring lucide'. No hex, palette class or arbitrary size was written anywhere on the screen.
